`rm`: remove files and directories.

## Synopsis

<strong>rm</strong> \[<strong>-r</strong>\] \[<strong>-f</strong>\] <em>path</em>...

## Description

<strong>rm</strong> removes each file named. A symbolic link is removed itself, never what it points to. A directory is removed only with <strong>-r</strong>.

## Options

Options may be combined (<strong>-rf</strong>) and may come anywhere among the paths.

<strong>-r -R</strong>
: Remove directories and everything in them. Links inside are removed, never followed.

<strong>-f</strong>
: Say nothing about paths that do not exist.

## Exit status

0 if everything named was removed (or, with <strong>-f</strong>, was not there); 1 otherwise, or for an unknown option.

## Notes

Any other option letter is refused (status 1, nothing removed). Any word starting with <strong>-</strong> is taken as options, so a file whose name starts with <strong>-</strong> must be named as <strong>./-name</strong>. There is no <strong>-i</strong> (no prompting).

## See also

<strong>rmdir</strong>(1), <strong>mv</strong>(1), <strong>find</strong>(1)
